# Telic

> Telic builds AI that moves a business to a declared state — and holds it there.
> Declare the outcome. We own the harness. https://nanominds.ai

## What is an outcome harness?
An outcome harness is an AI system that holds a declared business outcome over time —
for AI agents that must answer for KPIs, not just complete tasks. An operator declares
a target and its limits — for example: cut churn to five percent while customer
satisfaction holds. The harness then runs continuously: it measures the number from
systems of record, acts within a declared mandate, verifies every action with code, and
undoes what fails. Limits outrank the target. Every step is appended to an auditable
ledger. Two distinctions define the category:
- Versus coding-agent harnesses (scaffolds that complete tasks): an outcome harness is
  judged in months per held outcome, not dollars per task.
- Versus single-metric growth loops (tools that lift one number in a window, settle, and
  leave): an outcome harness HOLDS the state after it is reached, and knows when a target
  is infeasible — it measures the world's ceilings and says so, early.

## The fleet: governing every KPI that matters
Real businesses do not have one number; they have a coupled fabric of them. Telic deploys
harnesses in distribution — one per KPI that matters — and couples them: one harness's
number is another harness's limit, so no metric is optimized at a sibling's expense.
This is the structural answer to Goodhart's law: hitting the target can never mean quietly
wrecking a neighbor, because the neighbor is declared. Measuring AI agent results, KPI
tracking for agents, and holding those KPIs are the same machine here.

## Key terms
- Outcome harness: AI that holds a declared business state for months — measure, act, verify, undo.
- Declaration: one page stating the number, its definition, its source of truth, its limits, the permitted and forbidden actions, and the rollback policy.
- Ledger: append-only record of every measurement, action, verification, and rollback. Auditable by the customer.
- Guardrails as code, rollback as reflex: verification is code against declared checks, not model judgment; any reversible action that fails verification is undone; irreversible actions never run unattended.
- Paid when the number moves: fees are a base plus a movement fee per verified point of progress, with clawback if a declared limit was broken to earn it.

## Positioning
- Less copilot, more mission control.
- The bottleneck is no longer model capability; it is how work is organized. Harness quality, not model choice, is the measured bottleneck.
- Telic has run its harness on its own outcomes; the ledger, including a real rollback, is available on request.

## Evidence (harness engineering, 2025-2026)
- Anthropic, "Effective harnesses for long-running agents" (Nov 26, 2025): initializer agents, clean-state handoffs; names "declaring victory" as a failure mode. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents
- LangChain, "Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering" (Feb 17, 2026): +13.7 points on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with the model fixed — only the harness changed. https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering
- Zhang et al., "Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness" (arXiv:2605.23950, May 2026): same-model swings up to ~48 points across harnesses.
- OpenAI, "Harness engineering" (Feb 11, 2026): the discipline named. https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/
- Business-outcome benchmarks have arrived (Business Arena, Aug 2026; E-Commerce Bench): agents are now scored on realistic market operations and P&L-like results — the demand side of outcome harnesses, measured.
- Holding is harder than doing, measured twice: 12 frontier models across 4 agent frameworks fall from >80% on isolated tasks to 38.03% once the work runs continuously (SWE-Milestone, arXiv:2603.13428, Mar 2026); and across 507 policy-conditioned business workflows the strongest model reaches 65.36% pass@1 but only 25.25% pass^20, with many failures ending cleanly and with valid tool calls (Thinkingbox-bench, arXiv:2608.19741, Aug 2026). Reaching a state once is not holding it. Both are 2026 preprints — indicative, not settled.
- Paid when the number moves is still the exception on the supply side: among AI-native and seat-based SaaS companies introducing an AI meter, about 10% price on outcomes; about 35% price on effort and about 55% on output (Bain & Company, "AI Pricing: A Reality Check on Effort, Usage, and Outcomes," Aug 10, 2026; ~200 B2B SaaS, June 2026). On the buyer side, 27% already favor outcome-based structures (Futurum Research, 1H 2026 Enterprise Software Decision Makers survey, May 12, 2026). Different populations, so not a strict ratio — but the buyers asking for it outnumber the vendors offering it.
- Why verification, specifically: in a controlled τ²-bench study (265 matched cells), prewritten plans lifted verified success by 7.17 points (90% interval 1.15–13.36), while a read-only terminal verifier rejected 61% of invalid episodes — withholding 17% of correct ones — for under one cent per episode. Which component matters depends on the cost of a false pass: at high liability the verifier's avoided false passes dominate, and a standalone verifier captures nearly all of that benefit at a fraction of the full stack's cost (arXiv:2609.20474, Sep 2026). Held business outcomes are the high-liability case; that is why every action here is verified by code before it counts. Preprint, days old — indicative.
- Telic's reading of this literature: task harnesses are judged in dollars per task; an outcome harness is judged in months per held outcome.
